clue.text: I'd secret plan to be separate

indicators.note: to plan is to arrange or lay out, so the letters of the preceding words are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a secret scheme in order to stay apart from others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plan' reworks the letters of I'D and SECRET. Don't confuse DISCRETE (separate, distinct) with DISCREET (tactful).
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete things are distinct and individually separate from one another.

clue.text: Old treasure, an old penny short

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the old penny is taken away from the treasure

parts.note: a hoard is a hidden store of treasure
D was the abbreviation for a penny in Britain's pre-1971 currency

explanation.surface: Ancient treasure turns out to be a penny light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes D from HOARD; before 1971 British pennies were written d.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoar means grey with age, hence ancient or old, as in hoary.

clue.text: Opera sung by Miranda?

definitions.meaning: Bizet's opera about a Spanish gypsy
... Miranda was the Brazilian singer famous for her fruit hats, so this is her first name

explanation.walkthrough: Miranda looks like the Shakespeare heroine, but she is the singer Carmen Miranda.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmen is Bizet's opera and also the first name of the singer Miranda.

clue.text: Cricketer, British spinner? No, the complete opposite!

parts.note: an adman spins stories in advertisements, a person who puts spin on things

explanation.surface: A British spin bowler is described, then corrected as being the very reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The tag 'No, the complete opposite!' is a joke: Don Bradman was Australian, not British, and a batsman, not a spinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Donald Bradman was the great Australian batsman, the most famous cricketer of all.

clue.text: Miner clutches daughter, one involved in a crash

indicators.note: the miner holds the daughter, so the abbreviation goes inside his word

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: A miner holds his daughter tight, someone caught up in an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutches' puts D inside COLLIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A collider is something that collides, i.e. takes part in a crash or impact.

clue.text: Ordinary user of zebras

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means dull, commonplace
a zebra is a British striped road crossing, used by people on foot

explanation.walkthrough: A zebra crossing is a British pedestrian crossing marked with black and white stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian means dull and commonplace, and a pedestrian is a walker who uses zebra crossings.

clue.text: Cabling her was awkward

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters are clumsily jumbled

explanation.surface: Laying cables was an awkward job for her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges the letters of HER WAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick cable or rope used for mooring or towing ships.

clue.text: Creeping around is reptilian

indicators.note: creeping suggests the letters crawl about into a new order

explanation.surface: Something creeping about is like a reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creeping' signals the rearrangement. The definition is the noun sense: a reptilian is a reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinosaur was a prehistoric reptile, and a reptilian as a noun means a reptile.

clue.text: A threepenny performance?

parts.note: refers to the Brecht and Weill musical play whose English title names a cheap staged work

explanation.walkthrough: The Threepenny Opera is Brecht and Weill's 1928 work; threepence was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage work is titled The Threepenny Opera, so a threepenny performance is that musical drama.

clue.text: Something arborists care about?

indicators.note: about can mean around, turning the letters of the preceding word around

explanation.surface: Tree surgeons are interested in a certain thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CARE; the whole clue also reads as the definition, since an acer is a tree arborists look after.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the maple genus, a tree that tree surgeons tend.

clue.text: As in Egypt or the area around Jordan, say

definitions.text: As in Egypt or the area around Jordan, say

parts.words: As in Egypt or the area around Jordan, say
parts.note: the letters A and S sit in the centre of the word for a compass point, and Egypt and Jordan both lie in this region

explanation.walkthrough: One reading: 'As' are in the middle of EAST. The other: Egypt and Jordan are in that part of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The region spanning Egypt, Jordan and neighbouring states is called the Middle East.

clue.text: Admiral found in hold

definitions.meaning: Horatio ..., the British admiral killed at Trafalgar
a full or half ... is a wrestling grip

explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson is the famous British admiral and also a wrestling hold.

clue.text: Green mineral found in winding track

definitions.meaning: a dark green rock-forming mineral, often mottled
a snaking, twisting path or line

explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Serpentine is a green mineral, and as a noun a snaking, winding course.

clue.text: They listen to Chequers …

definitions.meaning: people who hear, as in an audience of listeners
read as checkers, people who inspect financial accounts

explanation.walkthrough: Chequers looks like the Prime Minister's country house; it is people who check (accounts). The ellipsis joins this to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditors are listeners, and also officials who check a company's accounts.

clue.text: … a quiet place for getting more rounds in?

definitions.meaning: a secluded refuge to withdraw to
read as ..., to buy everyone drinks again

explanation.walkthrough: A round is a set of drinks bought for a group in a British pub; to treat again is to buy another.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a quiet, secluded place, and to re-treat is to stand another round.

clue.text: Criminal enjoying a blaze of publicity!

definitions.text: Criminal enjoying a blaze of publicity!

parts.words: Criminal enjoying a blaze of publicity!
parts.note: the idiom blaze of publicity is taken literally: a lawbreaker who delights in starting fires

explanation.walkthrough: 'a blaze of publicity' means lots of attention, but here it is a literal fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-raiser who sets buildings ablaze is the criminal who would enjoy a literal blaze.

clue.text: Like lords wearing — er! — denim?

indicators.note: wearing means eroding or fraying, so the letters are worn into a new shape

explanation.surface: Picture peers, after a hesitant 'er', clad in jeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' looks like 'dressed in' but rearranges DENIM into MINED, placed after ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers wear robes trimmed with ermine fur, so lords are ermined.

clue.text: Amulet or another one that matches

indicators.note: another suggests a different version, so the letters are re-formed

explanation.surface: A charm or a second charm that is its twin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' rearranges AMULET OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An emulator imitates or equals something else, a rival that matches it.

clue.text: Runners organised in some schools

definitions.meaning: ability groups that pupils are sorted into in British schools

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, schools that 'stream' put pupils of similar ability in the same class.
explanation.definitionFit: Streams are brooks that run and also ability sets that pupils are divided into.

clue.text: Acrobatic leap performed around Taunton, say

definitions.meaning: an old variant spelling of the head-over-heels flip
Taunton is the county town of this southwest English county

explanation.walkthrough: Taunton is the county town of Somerset in southwest England. 'performed' links the definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is an old word for a somersault and the county containing Taunton.

clue.text: Royal house without an Aga?

parts.note: without is read as nothing, a zero, the letter O
an Aga is a British brand of range cooker

explanation.surface: A royal palace that lacks a fancy cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron range cooker, a status symbol in British country kitchens; 'without' supplies O, nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Orange is the Dutch royal dynasty, which gave England William III.

clue.text: Some birds in full flight? Wrong!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few birds flying in full formation is somehow wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'flight? Wrong' as definition; 'flight?' only completes the surface, and 'Wrong' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sinful is morally wrong, a transgression.

clue.text: One of Chekhov's trio, first in short series

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for first inside the shortened series

parts.note: SER is an abbreviation for series
first written 1st, with I standing for 1

explanation.surface: A Russian play's character starts off in a brief run of episodes.
explanation.walkthrough: Chekhov's play is Three Sisters. First is written 1st, and the 1 reads as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's Three Sisters are Olga, Masha and Irina, so one is a sister.

clue.text: They don't pull punches: one dying in hospital

indicators.note: in places the one dying inside the hospital's name

parts.note: Barts is St Bartholomew's Hospital in London
an ender is one that ends, i.e. dies

explanation.surface: Boxers who hit hard, one of whom is dying in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Barts is the London teaching hospital. Bar staff pull pints but merely mix and serve punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmen serve punch, the mixed drink, but they pull pints, not punches.

clue.text: A defensive all-rounder

parts.note: not a cricketer but a water-filled ditch that runs all round a castle to defend it

explanation.walkthrough: An all-rounder in cricket bats and bowls; here it means something that goes all around.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle's water-filled defensive ditch encircles it completely, going all round.

clue.text: Speck revealed by drug after test

indicators.note: after places the drug following the test

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles

explanation.surface: A tiny particle shows up after a drug test.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the yearly British safety test for cars over three years old.
explanation.definitionFit: A mote is a tiny particle, as of dust.

clue.text: Kelly's family inheritance?

definitions.meaning: belonging to Gene Kelly, the dancer of Singin' in the Rain
the hereditary units passed down through a family

explanation.walkthrough: Kelly's is read as the possessive of the actor's first name, Gene Kelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Genes are the hereditary units inherited from parents, and Gene's sounds the same.

clue.text: Woman sorts out the best players

parts.note: Mae is a woman's name, as in the actress Mae West

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman picks out the finest musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns the letters of 'sorts' into STROS. 'players' looks sporting but means musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestros are master musicians, the most eminent performers.
